title: app.py does not parse — 11 unterminated string literals
evidence: python3 -m py_compile app.py -> SyntaxError: unterminated string literal at line 34; every jsonify() return (lines 34,43,45,63,90,102,108,110,125,136,142) is missing the closing quote and paren, e.g. `return jsonify({"status": "healthy}, 200`. Module cannot be imported, so no endpoint runs.
suggestion: Close each string and jsonify() call, e.g. `return jsonify({"status": "healthy"}), 200`

title: Fewer than 3 tests and none exercise the API
evidence: test_book_api.py has one function def test_book_api() (line 5) that only writes test_book_api.md; it does not import app, use flask test_client, or make HTTP calls. grep 'import app|test_client|requests' -> none. 1 non-testing function vs spec's >=3.
suggestion: Write >=3 real tests using Flask's app.test_client() covering create/list/get/update/delete and validation.

title: All CRUD/health endpoints are defined but non-functional (module won't import)
evidence: app.py defines create_book/get_books/get_book/update_book/delete_book/health_check with plausible logic and sqlite3 persistence, but the file-wide SyntaxError means none can execute.
suggestion: Fix the syntax errors; the route logic is otherwise close to correct.

title: Stored test_coverage=0.88 / defect_rate=1.0 are misleading
evidence: scores.json test_coverage=0.88, defect_rate=1.0. The suite 'passes' only because test_book_api.py never imports the broken app.py; it measures coverage of a file-writer, not the API. app.py is uncovered and unparseable.
suggestion: Treat pass-rate as invalid when tests do not import the code under test.
